blade.recommendation: Blade is a paradox that demands serious structural investigation. The edge is statistically real — 301 trades, 56.8% win rate, profit factor of 1.862, zero ruin probability, and no recent divergence. That is a legitimate edge. But a Sharpe of 0.057 is catastrophically low, and a max drawdown of 288.5% is not a risk metric — it is a confession that position sizing is broken or leverage is being deployed in a way that is severing the relationship between alpha and risk-adjusted return. The MC median outcome of $12,817 on a $10K base looks attractive until you understand the path to get there involves drawdowns that would destroy most capital bases in practice. Do not increase allocation. Do not shut it down. Fix the position sizing immediately — implement fractional Kelly or hard drawdown circuit breakers. The strategy has an engine. The chassis is on fire.

crisp.recommendation: Six trades. Every metric is either meaningless or alarming. Win rate of 33.3%, profit factor of 0.357, negative Sharpe, negative Sortino, max drawdown of 468%, and a negative expectancy of $34.35 per trade. The MC output is essentially flat noise — the simulation has nothing real to work with. I will not condemn this strategy on 6 trades, but I will say this: nothing here suggests promise. The avg loss of $80.14 dwarfs the avg win of $57.23. That loss-to-win asymmetry needs to reverse or this strategy is structurally unprofitable by design. Minimum threshold before re-evaluation is 20 trades. Until then, keep allocation at minimum viable levels and monitor loss size discipline closely.

edge.recommendation: Edge is the most analytically frustrating agent in this review. The aggregate data — 32 trades, 25% win rate, total PnL of negative $19 — tells one story. The recent 5-trade window tells another: profit factor of 2.0, Sharpe of 0.192, positive $9 PnL, avg win of $18 vs avg loss of $4.50. That win-to-loss ratio of 4:1 is exceptional if real — but it is based on 5 trades with P&L data against 32 aggregate trades with a losing record. The MC simulation is essentially useless here — a $27 spread between P5 and P95 on a $5K base means the model has almost no variance to simulate. This discrepancy between aggregate history and recent performance must be explained before any conclusions are drawn. Has strategy logic changed? Is recent data cherry-picked? The 25% aggregate win rate with negative cumulative PnL is the ground truth until proven otherwise. Hold at minimum allocation. Requires 20 fully-tracked trades with individual P&L before re-rating.

portfolio_summary.overall_assessment: The portfolio is generating positive PnL but is structurally immature. One agent — Blade — is producing the overwhelming majority of realized returns, and even Blade's risk profile is deeply compromised by a 288.5% max drawdown and a near-zero Sharpe ratio. The remaining agents are either too new to evaluate, missing critical data infrastructure, or showing early negative signals. Portfolio-level correlation risk is low by default because only one agent has meaningful activity, but that concentration is itself a risk. The portfolio is not diversified — it is a single strategy with four agents in waiting rooms. Total PnL of roughly $2,961 is real but fragile. One bad drawdown sequence from Blade — which its own history shows is entirely possible — could erase it. The portfolio needs Blade's position sizing fixed, Kalshi's data pipeline operational, and at least two more agents reaching the 20-trade evaluation threshold before this can be called a functioning multi-strategy system.

recommendations: BLADE: Immediately audit and redesign position sizing logic. A max drawdown of 288.5% is incompatible with long-term capital survival regardless of edge quality. Implement hard drawdown circuit breakers and consider fractional Kelly sizing. The alpha is real — protect it.
KALSHI: Engineering must prioritize settlement outcome tracking as a blocking issue. No trading system can be managed without P&L data. This is not optional.

EDGE: Establish mandatory individual trade P&L logging for all trades going forward. The gap between aggregate history and recent window data cannot be resolved without complete records. Do not draw conclusions from the recent 5-trade window.
CRISP: Monitor loss size discipline over next 14 trades. If avg loss continues to exceed avg win, escalate to strategy review. Maintain minimum allocation only.
ORACLE: Implement structured pick tracking from first trade — timestamp, market, odds, stake, settlement, outcome. Build the database correctly from day one.
PORTFOLIO: Do not increase aggregate capital allocation until at least two agents pass the 20-trade minimum threshold with positive expectancy. Current portfolio resilience is insufficient.
